gaps.sentence: She goes to ___ school by bus every morning.
gaps.explanation: 'Go to school/work/bed/church' (as participant) takes no article.

gaps.sentence: We bought ___ antique mirror at the flea market.
gaps.explanation: 'An antique mirror' — 'antique' starts with a vowel sound.

gaps.sentence: We visited ___ Louvre on our last morning in Paris.
gaps.explanation: Most famous buildings and monuments take 'the': the Louvre, the Eiffel Tower.

gaps.sentence: ___ noise pollution in cities is getting worse.
gaps.explanation: 'Noise pollution' as a general concept takes no article.

gaps.sentence: He was ___ last person to leave the building.
gaps.explanation: Ordinals take 'the': the last person, the first time.

gaps.sentence: He was sent to ___ prison for armed robbery.
gaps.explanation: 'Be sent to prison' (as a prisoner) takes no article; visiting the building is 'go to the prison'.

gaps.sentence: She spent three weeks in ___ hospital after the accident.
gaps.explanation: British English: be in hospital (as a patient) takes no article; the building is the hospital.

gaps.sentence: The car crashed into a wall at ___ speed of 90 km/h.
gaps.explanation: 'At a speed of…' — 'a' is part of this fixed phrase.
